content:
Phase 68a implemented at b01183f (code at ec0cbe0; b01183f adds the evidence to the phase doc). gate: see entry @ b01183f.

What / where
- tagteam/watcher.py: the plan branch of _try_roadmap_advance is now _advance_plan_to_impl(state, project_dir) — same two staleness guards, same expected_seq write, same AUTO-ADVANCE line — called by full-roadmap as before and by _StateProcessor._handle_done when mode == 'headless', type plan, result approved AND state.get('run_mode', 'single-phase') == 'single-phase' (approval note 1: explicit, never inferred from _try_roadmap_advance returning None). That branch logs the done line, keeps the macOS notification, applies the transition and returns; the next tick dispatches the owed lead turn through the unchanged _handle_ready → engine.run_owed_turn. headless.py untouched. 'Sending completion notice…' is no longer printed by a headless watcher for any completion; tab/tmux/notify print and send exactly as before.
- Beat after tick: _beat_after_tick(project_dir) in the poll loop and the event loop's on_change re-reads the state and beats only when the new Sink.due() says a beat would be written (approval note 2: the beat carries the post-tick state; a short tick costs no write and no read).
- README headless section (the hand-off, where it stops, tagteam pause to read a plan first, no pickup after a restart), CLAUDE.md. Contract unchanged — it already says the lead is 'handed by the watcher after plan approval'.

Tests
- tests/test_watcher.py, 14 new against a real handoff-state.json: the advance (after a witnessed ready state, approval note 3) and the next tick running the lead's start-impl turn; first tick on an already-approved plan does nothing; no advance for impl approval, a non-approved result, full-roadmap without roadmap metadata, full-roadmap declined by a staleness guard; both guards; a lost seq race; pause holds the advanced turn and resume dispatches it once; iterm2/tmux/notify unchanged incl. the typed message; full-roadmap still advances through the shared helper. 9 of the 14 fail on the previous watcher.py (checked by swapping the file); the other 5 pin unchanged behaviour.
- tests/test_watchlog.py: a long tick (poll and event loop) leaves a beat from after it carrying the state the tick produced; a short tick writes no second beat and re-reads nothing.
- Focused: test_watchlog, test_watcher, test_headless, test_watcher_lock, test_watcher_events = 274 passed, 1 skipped.

Criterion 8, real processes (manual, log in the phase doc): scratch project, plan opened by hand, then only 'tagteam watch --mode headless --pidfile' → reviewer approved the plan → advance → the lead's turn ran as a cycle turn (not a conversation), implemented and opened the impl cycle → reviewer approved → impl/done/approved in 2m15s with no click and no cockpit; python3 test_wc.py → 6 passed (run by hand). watch status sampled every 3 s through the run and 18 s after: 39 samples, 0 STALE (the pre-fix trial showed one). One run: an observation, not a rate.

Not verified: the event-loop beat path with a real watchdog observer (headless forces the poll loop; covered by the modelled test only).

GATE: PASS | scope 6 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2219 passed, 5 skipped, 7m43s)
checked: HEAD b01183f

Approved implementation at b01183f (code ec0cbe0). The shared helper preserves the existing staleness guards and expected-seq write. The new caller explicitly restricts advancement to headless single-phase approved plans; full-roadmap declines cannot fall through into it. The transition leaves dispatch to the ordinary next tick, so pause/resume and engine start-command verification remain in force. Existing first-poll behavior, terminal completion notices, and terminal single-phase impl approval are preserved.

The post-tick heartbeat re-reads state only when due and uses the existing beat throttle under its lock. Focused tests cover long ticks in both loops carrying the new state, short-tick read/write suppression, the sequence race, restart, full-roadmap boundaries, and pause/resume dispatch once. Sink.due is a small justified addition supporting the approved heartbeat requirement.

Verification: reviewer tests/test_watcher.py + tests/test_watchlog.py: 115 passed. git diff --check 3a54c92..HEAD clean. Gate PASS at b01183f: 2219 passed, 5 skipped; accepted without rerunning the suite. The phase doc records the real scratch-project reviewer → lead implementation → reviewer run without a click and 39 status samples with no STALE result. The new event-loop heartbeat path has modeled coverage, not a new real-watchdog manual run; this limitation is accurately disclosed and is not a blocker for this small shared callback change.

No outstanding findings or interjections. The README explains automatic plan-to-impl handoff, pause, restart behavior, and the single-phase stopping point.
